data: Most massive known dwarf planet — slightly smaller than Pluto by radius but ~27% more massive. Its 2005 discovery prompted the IAU to formalise the 'dwarf planet' category in 2006, simultaneously demoting Pluto. Lies in the scattered disk on a highly inclined, eccentric orbit reaching past 97 AU at aphelion.
Eris's 44° orbital inclination is among the highest of any catalogued large body — its scattered-disc origin puts it well off the ecliptic.
Eris swings from 38 AU at perihelion to 97 AU at aphelion — a ~68-AU mean orbit (semi-major axis). It passed aphelion around 1977 and is now slowly moving back toward the Sun.
The tilt of the orbit plane relative to a reference plane — usually the ecliptic or Earth's equator.
The two extreme points on every elliptical orbit: closest approach, and farthest.
